questions.question: The Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajaraja I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brihadeswara Temple **at **Tanjavur **was built by **Rajaraja I**.
 
• Rajaraja I was a prominent ruler of the Chola dynasty in South India.
 
• The temple, also known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil**, is a Hindu temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva**.
 
• It is one of the largest temples in India and is an outstanding example of Tamil architecture during the Chola period.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **magnificent vimana** (tower) and **intricate sculptures**.
 
• It was completed in **1010 AD **and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, recognized for its historical and architectural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajaraja I** ruled from **985 AD to 1014 AD** and expanded the Chola Empire significantly during his reign.
 
• He is credited with establishing a strong administration and commissioning several architectural projects, including the Brihadeswara Temple.
 
• The temple's construction marked the height of Chola architectural and cultural achievements.
 
• Rajaraja I's reign is often considered a **golden period in South Indian history**, known for advancements in art, architecture, and literature.
 
• The temple's design and construction techniques continue to be studied and admired by historians and architects around the world.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Cholas?

1 The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore.

2 Vikram Chola had in his veins the blood of the Cholas and Eastern Chalukyas.

3 Rajendra I Chola is known as Gangaikonda Chola.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore (Thanjavur):** Thanjavur served as the political, cultural, and religious center of the Chola Empire.
 
• **Vikram Chola's lineage:** Vikram Chola, a notable ruler of the Chola dynasty, was a descendant of both the Cholas and the Eastern Chalukyas, showcasing the dynastic alliances of the period.
 
• **Gangaikonda Chola:** Rajendra I Chola earned the title "Gangaikonda Chola" after his victorious expedition to the Ganges River, symbolizing his expansionist policies.
 
• The Cholas were known for their contributions to art, architecture, and administration, with temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple standing as a testament to their legacy.
 
• The Chola dynasty played a significant role in maritime trade and had extensive influence in Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Administration:** The Cholas implemented an efficient administrative system, including well-organized village assemblies (sabhas) that managed local affairs.
 
• **Temple Architecture:** The Cholas are renowned for their monumental temple architecture, especially the Brihadeeswarar Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **Naval Power:** The Chola Empire had a powerful navy, enabling them to establish trade and cultural ties with Southeast Asia, including the Srivijaya Empire.
 
• **Literary Contributions:** The Chola period saw significant advancements in Tamil literature, with works like Kamba Ramayanam being composed during their reign.
 
• **Gangaikonda Cholapuram:** Rajendra I established Gangaikonda Cholapuram as a new capital to commemorate his conquests and to signify the Chola Empire's dominance.

questions.question: ______ was the capital of the Pandya dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Madurai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pandya kingdom was a Tamil kingdom in South India.
 
• Madurai __was the capital of the__ Pandyan dynasty__ until the middle of the 14th century and __Korkai __was also the__ capital and port city of Pandya.__
 
• The third capital was Tenkasi until the end of the 16th century.
 
• The Pandyas revived under Kadungon (590 – 620 CE) towards the end of the 6th century, helped to disestablish the Kalabhras in south India.
 
• The Pandya dynasty was amongst the three ancient Tamil dynasties, the Cheras and Cholas being the other two.
 
• The early Pandyas ruled the southern part of India from 4th century BCE and their rule ended in the 16th century BCE.
 
• The Empire was also home to temples such as Nellaiappar temple in Tirunelveli and Meenakshi Amman temple in Madurai. Vaishnavism, Shaivism, and Jainism also flourished during the reign of the early Pandya kings.

questions.question: Rajaraja I, the most powerful Chola ruler, became king in ______ C.E.

__
 
• Rajaraja I, a Chola emperor, ruled between 985 and 1014 CE.
 
• He is known for restoring the Chola hegemony and securing its dominance throughout the Indian Ocean during his time as the most powerful Tamil king in South India.
 
• He ruled over a sizable portion of northern Sri Lanka, the Chera country, and the Pandya country.
 
• Also, he bought Lakshadweep, the Thiladhunmadulu atoll, and a portion of the Maldives' northernmost islands in the Indian Ocean.

• For over 500 years, they were able to maintain their hegemony.
 
 
 
• Pandya:
 
 
• ​The Pandyan dynasty, commonly known as the Pandyas of Madurai, was one of the three major kingdoms of Tamilakam, or South India, together with the Chera and Chola dynasties.
 
 
 
• Chalukya:
 
 
• ​During the sixth through the twelfth centuries, the Chalukya dynasty, a Classical Indian monarchy, ruled over a sizable portion of southern and central India.

questions.question: "Brahmadeya" a type of land during Chola Period was the ______.

options.text: land of non - Brahmana peasant proprietors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**land gifted to Brahmans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Chola period, "Brahmadeya" **was a type of **land that was gifted to Brahmans **as a form of religious endowment.
 
• This land was considered sacred and was exempt from taxes and other obligations.
 
• The purpose of such endowments was to ensure the welfare of the Brahmans and to earn religious merit for the donors.
 
• The other options are not correct because "land of non-Brahmana peasant proprietors" was known as "grama" and was subject to taxes and other obligations. "Land gifted to temples" was known as "devadana" and was also exempt from taxes but was not exclusively for Brahmans. "Land of royal person" was known as "rajakulam" and was under the control of the king.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Brahmans were the highest caste in the Hindu social hierarchy and were traditionally associated with priestly and scholarly roles.
 
• Religious endowments were a common practice in ancient India and were used to support various religious institutions and individuals.
 
• The practice of Brahmans receiving land as endowments continued well into the medieval period and beyond.
 
• The concept of "Brahmadeya" reflects the importance of land as a form of wealth and power in ancient India.

questions.question: Vetti tax is the most frequently mentioned tax in the inscription of Cholas who ruled in Tamil Nadu. This tax was taken in the form of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**forced labour.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vetti Tax:-**

 
 
• **It was a form of forced labor tax levied by the Chola dynasty in southern India. (Hence Option 4 is correct)**
 
• It was the most frequently mentioned tax in Chola inscriptions.
 
• Under the Vetti system, common people were forced to work for the king or their village landlords without any wages.
 
• The Vetti tax was used for a variety of purposes, such as construction and maintenance of public works, such as roads, irrigation systems, and temples.
 
• It was also used to support the military and the royal court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other various taxes imposed by the Chola dynasty:-
 
 
• **Land tax (Kadamai):** This was the most important tax, and was levied on all agricultural land. The rate of tax varied depending on the type of crop and the quality of the land.
 
• **House tax (Manaiya):** This was a tax levied on all houses, regardless of their size or value.
 
• **Market tax (Shulka)**: This was a tax levied on all goods bought and sold in markets.
 
• **Professional tax (Pesha):** This was a tax levied on people who practiced certain professions, such as merchants, artisans, and doctors.
